text:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression on paged-attn at long sequences (1.5k-2k). spikes in generation latency correlate with frequent compaction runs and big memcpy bursts. reproducible on ded-dev cluster.

perf-bot: summary from the run on gcu-12: memory churn ~1.1 GB/s, compaction events=7, avg compaction latency=48ms, peak memcpy 320MB/s, tail P95 latency +18%. logs/snippet below.

perf-bot: ```
[profile] run=2026-03-15 model=redwood-open-attn seq=2048 steps=60
kernels: paged_attn_v2 (80%), streaming_attn (20% fallback)
compactions: 7 total, total_ms=338, avg_ms=48
memcpy: total_mb=1240, peak_mb_s=320
KV cache hits: 72%, hot-prefix reuse: low
```

mauro: hmm. looks like compaction is doing full-page memcpy more often than expected. I suspect our threshold for marking free ranges as reclaimable is too aggressive — causes lots of small free segments -> increased fragmentation -> more compaction.

linh: agreed. also seeing that workspace per-inference gets resized aggressively when batching heuristics change, which triggers allocator churn. two levers: 1) soften workspace shrink hysteresis, 2) increase block reuse bucket size to absorb transient bursts.

anya: can we try a quick experiment: double the reuse_bucket for 16KB/64KB block classes and set workspace shrink cooldown to 10s (was 1s)? if that reduces compaction rate we keep; if not revert.

sam: +1. also propose kernel fallback rule: when fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 AND compaction_rate > 2/min, prefer streaming kernel (lower memory working set) until fragmentation drops. should avoid OOMs during compaction storms.

linh: sketch of heuristic pseudocode:
```
frag = free_gaps_bytes / total_managed_bytes
if frag > 0.35 and compactions_last_min > 2:
  kernel = streaming_attn_kernel
else:
  kernel = paged_attn_kernel
```

mauro: note: streaming kernel increases per-token compute slightly but avoids ~50-200ms compaction stalls (observed). tactical tradeoff for tail latency.

perf-bot: ran a 10-min A/B with proposed settings (reuse_bucket x2, shrink_cooldown=10s, kernel-rule enabled): compaction events dropped from 7->1 in the trace, memcpy total_mb down 1240->210, P95 latency improved by ~12%.

anya: sweet. please push a small canary config to dedicated-canary and run mixed-load for 2 hours. we need to validate under high-concurrency (200rps).

sam: one more thought — background incremental compaction: instead of doing full-page compaction inline, schedule small async compaction tasks on a low-priority CUDA stream that yield frequently. reduces blocking but increases GPU scheduling churn. worth trying if background IO is cheap.

linh: implementing incremental compaction will require changes in blockmgr: mark pages "pending-compact" and let compactor operate with batch size limit and time-slice. I can prototype.

mauro: also let's add a perf counter: compaction_bytes_attempted vs compaction_bytes_moved. we can detect wasted compaction (low bytes moved) and back off automatically.

anya: action items: (1) sam/mauro deploy canary config with reuse_bucket & cooldown, kernel-rule, (2) linh prototype incremental compactor branch, (3) perf-bot run 2h mixed-load and post results here.

sam: marking follow-up in tracker: INT-1374 reclaim/batching/canary. I'll attach diff when ready. :white_check_mark:

linh: will open PR with prototype flags under feature/async-compact. expect draft tomorrow.

perf-bot: scheduled mixed-load job to start in 2h, will ping with results.

anya: thanks everyone — big win if can drop compaction spikes. let's avoid changing allocator algorithm (slab->buddy) for now; try heuristics first.

mauro: fwiw we should still run one offline sim of slab vs buddy fragmentation on synthetic workload (vary prefix reuse, request sizes) to quantify long-term tradeoffs. I'll volunteer to run it.

sam: ack. ping me with the canary config and I'll roll. :rocket:
